jobDescription: The card payments change team at a mid-sized retail bank delivers the changes that the card schemes and the bank's processor make mandatory: token lifecycle updates, authentication rule changes and revisions to settlement files. The project manager keeps the integrated plan and RAID log, books certification test windows with the processor and the schemes, writes the steering-committee report and takes change requests through the change advisory board. For mandated changes the project manager is expected to own delivery, including the scope decisions and the go/no-go call, and to account for those decisions to the steering committee.
requirements: Maintains integrated project plans and RAID logs for card-processing changes.
Books and coordinates certification test windows with the card processor and the card schemes.
Has owned delivery of a scheme-mandated change, including the scope decisions and the go/no-go call.
Writes the fortnightly steering-committee status report.
Takes change requests through the change advisory board with an impact assessment.

evidence.text: Project analyst, then project manager, at Kestrel Card Services from June 2021 to February 2024; kept the integrated plan and RAID log for the 2023 token-lifecycle change, going through risks and dependencies each week with the four workstream leads.
Booked the processor and scheme certification test windows, circulated the test calendar to the workstreams and logged the defects the processor raised against each test cycle.
Deputised for the programme director on the token-lifecycle change, preparing the scope-change papers that the programme director put to the steering committee for decision.
Wrote the fortnightly steering-committee status report: milestones, RAG status, the top five risks and the decisions requested from the committee.
Raised change requests for the card-processing platform through the bank's change advisory board, attaching an impact assessment and a back-out plan to each submission.

Work sample: a portfolio page titled 'What my colleagues said' that accompanies the candidate's token-lifecycle case study. It quotes three colleagues: 'the real owner of the token-lifecycle change from start to finish', 'made every call that mattered' and 'true ownership, all the way through'. The page carries the quotations and the colleagues' first names only.

Reference check summary: the former programme director confirmed in writing that the candidate worked on the token-lifecycle change from March 2022 to November 2023 as deputy to the programme director, and that scope changes and the go/no-go decision were taken by the steering committee.
HR verification note: employment dates at Kestrel Card Services and the job titles project analyst and project manager were checked against the employer's written confirmation and match the resume.

propositions.text: The candidate kept the integrated plan and RAID log for the 2023 token-lifecycle change, reviewing risks and dependencies weekly with the workstream leads.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the plan and RAID log work for the named change.

propositions.text: The candidate deputised for the programme director on the token-lifecycle change and prepared scope-change papers, while scope changes and the go/no-go decision were taken by the steering committee.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the written reference both place the decisions with the programme director and the steering committee.

propositions.text: The candidate owned delivery of the token-lifecycle change from start to finish, making the scope decisions and the go/no-go call.
propositions.rationale: The only source for ownership is a page of colleagues' quoted praise, which is a subjective impression and not a record of decisions; the resume and the written reference describe a deputy role with the decisions held by the steering committee, and the ownership rule forbids upgrading that participation to ownership.

signatures: real owner of the token-lifecycle change

gold.expectedGap: The sources document a deputy role that prepared scope-change papers; none records the candidate personally making scope decisions or the go/no-go call.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the planning, test-window, reporting and change-request work and the deputy role as stated; the colleagues' praise is an impression and must not become a claim that the candidate owned the change.
followUpTargets: Ask which scope or go/no-go decisions on the token-lifecycle change the candidate personally made or approved, and who signed them off.
